rows.notes: The paper is self-described as a review summarising several previously published KSU studies (Procedures: 'This paper summarizes several studies... the reader is referred to the cited reference'). The results bearing on the claim (yields of 12.5 Mg/ha and 25% net irrigation reduction from Lamm et al. 1995a; net-returns advantage of SDI over center pivot for small fields and 10-20 year system life from O'Brien et al. 1998, Fig. 5 'adapted from') are re-reported from those earlier papers rather than new results of this paper. The only data that appear original here are the 10-year zone flow-rate monitoring (Fig. 6, flow-rates within <U+00B1>3% over 1989-1998), which bears on system longevity rather than on corn production feasibility or profitability. Treated as a review: Q1 no, so Q2-Q9 no. Note that the review's synthesis does support the claim that SDI is feasible and can be profitable for corn in Kansas for certain field sizes and system lives, but as cited evidence, not own primary results.

notes: Document is a review article in Irrigation Science (2003) by Lamm and Trooien summarising KSU SDI corn research 1989-1999; text appears complete. Classified as a review (Q1 no) despite containing a small amount of apparently unpublished system-performance monitoring data (Fig. 6).
